title: Overfitting and regularization
text: Overfitting happens when a model learns noise and quirks of the training data instead of the underlying pattern, so it scores well on training data but poorly on new data. The usual sign is training error that keeps falling while validation error rises. Common remedies: get more or more varied data; reduce model complexity (fewer parameters, shallower trees); add regularization such as L1 or L2 penalties, which discourage large weights; use dropout in neural networks; stop training early when validation loss stops improving; and use cross-validation to get a more reliable estimate of performance. Underfitting is the opposite problem: the model is too simple to capture the pattern, so both training and validation error stay high.

title: SQL joins
text: A join combines rows from two tables based on a related column. INNER JOIN returns only rows with a match in both tables. LEFT JOIN returns every row from the left table, with matching columns from the right table or NULL when there is no match; it is useful for questions like 'all customers and their orders, including customers with no orders'. RIGHT JOIN is the mirror image. FULL OUTER JOIN returns all rows from both sides, filling NULLs where either side has no match. A common mistake is filtering a LEFT JOIN's right-hand table in the WHERE clause, which silently turns it back into an inner join; put that condition in the ON clause instead.

title: The STAR method for behavioral answers
text: STAR is a structure for answering behavioral questions. Situation: briefly set the context, such as the team, project and stakes. Task: state what you specifically were responsible for. Action: describe the steps you personally took, using 'I' rather than 'we', and explain why you chose them. Result: give the outcome, quantified where possible, and what you learned. Strong answers spend most of their time on Action and Result, pick one specific real event rather than a general habit, and stay around two minutes long. Weak answers stay vague, describe what the team did without the candidate's own role, or stop without a result.
